correctness.rationale: A valid perfect-matching objective follows from one use per label. The 2025 marginal binomial-mixture identity fixes means and variances. Uniform Fourier lattice local limits and Hoeffding concentration yield each interior column maximum; endpoint binomial peak estimates show removed boundary columns are negligible. A block-interleaved permutation attains the matching coefficient by local limits and Riemann sums. Its integral is evaluated exactly. A standalone standard-library checker passes 61 finite exact-rational/assignment groups; these complement rather than substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2025 marginal-mixture result and 2026 fixed-shuffle sequel both permit repeated guesses and maximize independently over positions. This theorem uses a bijective strategy constraint and obtains a different asymptotic coefficient via a sharp column-capacity upper bound and a matching constructive assignment. The older one-shuffle limit-law article likewise uses repeat guesses. Available published-result profiles and web searches did not identify a covering equivalent. Priority remains provisional; missing historical coverage is a residual risk.

value.rationale: Using every label exactly once is a natural, globally coupled version of no-feedback guessing; the usual repeated-guess row maxima do not solve it. An explicit fixed-k sharp constant and readily implemented matching determine its asymptotic cost. One riffle gives sqrt(2/pi), strictly below 2/sqrt(pi) for unrestricted repeat guesses. This is a structural optimization result rather than a small finite numerical improvement.
